name: Tessera Industries Void Grenade VG-1 'Black Hole'
description: An experimental ordnance device that creates a 2-meter sphere of spatial compression lasting 0.5 seconds — everything within the sphere is subjected to extreme compressive forces as space itself contracts, crushing matter into a fraction of its original volume before the effect collapses and space snaps back to normal. The result is a sphere of mangled, compressed debris where intact objects used to be. Tessera's physicists describe it as a 'controlled spatial anomaly' and freely admit they do not fully understand the long-term effects on local spacetime. The Void Grenade is the single most classified item in Tessera's research division, and its existence has been confirmed only by the distinctive spherical compression signatures found at two classified incident sites.
specifications: effect radius: 2-meter sphere effect duration: 0.5 seconds compression force: Estimated 50,000 atmospheres within sphere detonation: 3-second timer after activation weight: 0.5 kg form factor: Standard grenade size prototypes: Estimated 5 units manufactured side effects: Unknown long-term spacetime distortion classification: Tessera Ultra-Restricted
story_hooks: A crime scene contains a perfect 2-meter sphere of crushed, compressed matter — vehicles, building material, and three human bodies reduced to a dense ball. Nothing in any weapons database explains it.

A Tessera researcher involved in the VG-1 program has disappeared after sending encrypted messages claiming the spatial compression events are not contained — each detonation is leaving a permanent microscopic weakness in spacetime that could accumulate.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deceptively simple sphere that seems to absorb light around its surface — matte obsidian-black with a subtle iridescent shimmer at certain angles, as if reality itself is slightly bent around it. The grenade body is perfectly smooth and featureless except for a single recessed activation button at the north pole. No ridges, no fins, no traditional safety mechanisms — it looks more like a physicist's theoretical model than a weapon.
physical_description.dimensions: 11 cm diameter sphere. Activation button recessed 0.3 cm. Total weight maintains center of gravity despite internal void-generation matrices.
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly light for its volume — approximately 500 grams. Feels almost buoyant in the palm, as if the object itself is subtly pushing away from normal space. Density is uneven; the interior seems to shift slightly when tilted.
physical_description.primary_material: Tessera's proprietary 'Null-Alloy' composite — a layered matrix of tungsten carbide microstructure bonded with exotic matter stabilizers. The outer shell is a non-reflective polymer coating over the composite core.
physical_description.finish: Matte obsidian black with microscopic surface irregularities. Under close inspection, faint concentric circles are visible — manufacturing seams where the sphere was assembled in sections. A thin iridescent oil-slick shimmer plays across the surface under any light source, suggesting internal fields are already active at a minimal level.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: absolute matte black. Accents: hairline traces of deep purple at the edges of the recessed activation button, suggesting active energy pathways just beneath the surface.
physical_description.grip_texture: Smooth and subtly warm — almost too smooth, unnaturally frictionless polymer coating. The activation button is textured with three shallow grooves for positive identification in darkness, and carries a faint electric tingle when touched.
distinctive_features: Perfectly spherical form with no traditional grenade ridges or safety lever
Single recessed activation button at the north pole with purple energy traces
Concentric manufacturing seams barely visible on the surface
Subtle iridescent shimmer suggesting active containment fields
Microscopic pulsing near the core — visible only in low-light conditions as a faint violet glow
No visible serial numbers or manufacturer markings (deniable asset)
Surface temperature remains constant at 19°C regardless of ambient conditions
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Deliberately absent. However, microscopic etching on the interior of the activation button reads 'TI-VG1-Φ' in Tessera's proprietary font — only visible if disassembled, which no one who has attempted has returned to report.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine and inert. Each unit is stored in a Faraday-lined containment case with active stabilization fields. Field-deployed units show signs of extreme stress — hairline fractures in the polymer coating, discoloration from proximity to energy sources, and subtle warping of the sphere's geometry from spatial pressure.
